title: CONSUMER COOPERATIVES ACT
full_text:
CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Act is to contribute to improving the livelihood of cooperative members as consumers and promoting the welfare and lifestyles of citizens by encouraging activities of cooperatives that jointly purchase, use, and sell goods, service, facilities, etc. in an independent, self-supporting, and autonomous manner based on mutual cooperation among consumers in a spirit of mutual assistance. <Amended on Dec. 7, 2021>

Article 2 (Definitions) The terms used in this Act are defined as follows:
  1. The term "cooperative" means a consumer cooperative established pursuant to this Act in order to accomplish the purpose specified in Article 1;
  2. The term "federation" means a federation of consumer cooperatives established pursuant to this Act in order to promote common interests of the cooperatives;
  3. The term "national federation" means a national federation of consumer cooperatives established pursuant to this Act in order to promote common interests of cooperatives and federations.

Article 3 (Corporate Personality and Address) (1) A cooperative, a federation, and a national federation shall be a non-profit corporation.
  (2) The principal place of business of a cooperative, a federation, or a national federation shall be its seat.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Dec. 7, 2021]

Article 4 (Name) (1) A cooperative, a federation, or a national federation (hereinafter referred to as "cooperative or federation") shall use either "consumer cooperative" or "consumer co-op" in its name.
  (2) No person, other than a cooperative or federation established pursuant to this Act, shall use "consumer cooperative," "consumer co-op," or any similar word in its name.
  (3) A cooperative engaging in health and medical services to improve the health of its members pursuant to Article 45 (1) 4 (hereinafter referred to as “health and medical cooperative”) shall indicate the fact that its own medical institution has been founded by a cooperative, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Prime Minister. <Newly Inserted on Mar. 29, 2016>

Article 5 (Business Territory) (1) The business territory of a cooperative shall be stipulated in its articles of incorporation, taking into consideration administrative districts, administrative boundaries of its inhabitants, etc., as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (2) The business territory of a federation shall be stipulated in its articles of incorporation and may be nationwide.
  (3) The business territory of a national federation shall be nationwide.

Article 6 (Basic Principles) (1) A cooperative or federation shall make an utmost effort to serve a cooperative member or a member cooperative or federation when conducting its business. <Newly Inserted on Dec. 7, 2021>
  (2) Except as otherwise provided in this Act, a cooperative or federation shall meet the following requirements: <Amended on Dec. 7, 2021>
  1. It shall not aim at profit-making, but instead aim to encourage mutual assistance among cooperative members or member cooperatives or federations;
  2. Every cooperative member or every member cooperative or federation shall have an equal voting right on resolutions and in elections, irrespective of the number of equity shares: Provided, That a federation or a national federation may give unequal voting rights to its member cooperatives or federations according to the number of cooperative members belonging to a member cooperative or federation, as stipulated by its articles of incorporation.
  (3) No cooperative or federation shall engage in business only for the interests of a specific cooperative member or a specific member cooperative or federation. <Amended on Dec. 7, 2021>
  [Title Amended on Dec. 7, 2021]

Article 7 (Prohibition of Involvement in Election of Public Officials) (1) No cooperative or federation shall engage in any activity to support or oppose a specific political party in the election of a public official or any activity to make a specific person succeed or fail in an election.
  (2) No person shall use a cooperative or federation to engage in any activity specified in paragraph (1).

Article 8 (Responsibilities of Cooperatives or Federations) (1) A cooperative or federation shall fully engage in such activities as providing education, training, or information to enhance the rights and interests of cooperative members or member cooperatives or federations.
  (2) A cooperative or federation shall endeavor to promote the production and distribution of environment-friendly products, to encourage mutually beneficial relations between producers and consumers (applicable only to non-health and medical cooperatives), and to provide appropriate health and medical services (applicable only to health and medical cooperatives).
  (3) A cooperative or federation shall endeavor to promote the sustainable development of local communities, to create quality jobs, and to conserve the environment and natural ecosystem.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Dec. 7, 2021]

Article 9 (Cooperation of the State) (1) The State, local governments, schools at various levels (referring to the schools under the Elementary and Secondary Education Act and the Higher Education Act), and public organizations (hereafter in this Article referred to as the "State, etc.") shall fully cooperate with cooperatives or federations in their business activities, and may subsidize such business activities. <Amended on Dec. 7, 2021>
  (2) The State, etc. may provide cooperatives or federations with facilities and commodities of the State, etc. for their use. <Amended on Dec. 7, 2021>
  (3) The State, etc. may exempt a cooperative or federation that directly uses state-owned property, public property, or commodities for the purpose of promoting consumers' welfare from fees for using such property or commodities, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Dec. 7, 2021>
  (4) The State, etc. shall hear the opinions of cooperatives or federations and shall endeavor to reflect such opinions. <Amended on Dec. 7, 2021>
  [Title Amended on Dec. 7, 2021]

Article 9-2 (Formulation of Policies on Cooperatives) The Fair Trade Commission shall formulate and implement a development plan for revitalizing cooperatives every three years, and to that end, may examine the current status and actual conditions of cooperatives in cooperation with cooperatives or federations.
  [This Article Newly Inserted on Dec. 7, 2021]

Article 10 (Cooperation with Other Cooperatives or Federations) A cooperative or federation shall endeavor to promote mutual cooperation and understanding with other cooperatives or federations, cooperatives under other statutes, and foreign cooperatives, and the development of joint projects therewith.

Article 11 (Relationship to Other Statutes) (1) Article 19 of the Grain Management Act and Article 56 of the Trucking Transport Business Act shall not apply to business activities of a cooperative or federation.
  (2) The Insurance Business Act shall not apply to mutual aid programs of a federation or a national federation.
  (3) This Act shall take precedence over relevant Acts with regard to health and medical services of a cooperative or federation.

Article 12 (Application Mutatis Mutandis of Other Statutes) The provisions of the Civil Act governing incorporated associations shall apply mutatis mutandis to cooperatives or federation, except as provided in this Act. In such cases, "incorporated association" shall be construed as "cooperative," "federation," "national federation"; "partner" as "cooperative member," "member cooperative or federation"; and "permission" as "authorization," respectively.

CHAPTER II COOPERATIVE

SECTION 1 Cooperative Members

Article 13 (Qualification for Membership) In order to be qualified for membership in a cooperative, a person shall have his or her domicile, abode, place of business, or workplace within the business territory of the cooperative.

Article 14 (Accession) Without good cause, no cooperative shall refuse to admit a person as a cooperative member or require any person to comply with unfavorable conditions in admitting the person as a member, compared to other cooperative members.

Article 15 (Investment) (1) A cooperative member shall contribute at least one unit, as stipulated by articles of incorporation: Provided, That a member may make his or her contribution in kind, if necessary, as stipulated by articles of incorporation.
  (2) The number of contribution units per member shall not exceed 20/100 of the total number of contribution units.
  (3) The payment that shall be made to a cooperative for equity shares shall not be offset against a claim receivable from the cooperative.
  (4) A cooperative member's liability shall be limited to the amount paid by him or her for equity shares.

Article 16 (Voting Rights on Resolutions or in Elections) (1) Each cooperative member shall have one vote on a resolution or in an election, irrespective of the number of his or her contribution units.
  (2) A cooperative member may exercise his or her voting right on a resolution or in an election by proxy. In such cases, the member shall be deemed to be present at the meeting.
  (3) A proxy under paragraph (2) shall be another cooperative member or a family member who cohabits with the principal (referring to the spouse of a cooperative member, a lineal ascendant or descendent or a sibling of a cooperative member or his or her spouse, or the spouse of a lineal ascendant or descendent or a sibling of a cooperative member; hereinafter the same shall apply), and the number of cooperative members for whom a person can act as proxy shall be limited to one person.
  (4) A proxy under paragraph (2) shall submit a document certifying his or her power of proxy to the cooperative, as stipulated by its articles of incorporation.

Article 17 (Apportionment and Collection of Expenses) (1) A cooperative may impose on, and collect from its members, expenses, penalties, use charges, fees (hereinafter referred to as "expenses, etc."), as stipulated by its articles of incorporation.
  (2) Expenses, etc. payable by a cooperative member shall not be offset against a claim receivable from the cooperative.

Article 18 (Withdrawals) (1) A cooperative member may withdraw from the cooperative by giving notice that he or she intends to opt out.
  (2) A cooperative member shall be automatically withdrawn from the cooperative in any of the following cases: <Amended on Mar. 29, 2016>
  1. Where the cooperative member is no longer qualified for membership;
  2. Where the cooperative member dies;
  3. Where the cooperative member is declared a person under adult guardianship.

Article 19 (Expulsion) (1) If a cooperative member falls under any of the following cases, the cooperative may expel the cooperative member upon resolution passed at a general meeting:
  1. Where the cooperative member has not used the cooperative's business services for at least the period specified in its articles of incorporation;
  2. Where the cooperative member does not fulfill his or her obligation to pay his or her investment in equity shares or expenses, etc. or any other obligation to the cooperative;
  3. Where the cooperative member interferes with the cooperative's business services or engages in any activity to degrade the cooperative's credibility;
  4. Where the cooperative member engages in any other activity prohibited by its articles of incorporation.
  (2) When a cooperative intends to expel a cooperative member pursuant to paragraph (1), it shall notify the cooperative member of the reasons therefor at least 10 days before opening a general meeting and shall provide him or her with an opportunity to express his or her opinion at the general meeting.
  (3) No cooperative shall have any valid defense to protest against a cooperative member expelled in accordance with a resolution passed at a general meeting to expel the member without giving the member an opportunity to express his or her opinion under paragraph (2).

Article 20 (Right to Request Refund of Equity Shares) (1) A cooperative member withdrawn or expelled from a cooperative may request the cooperative to refund his or her equity shares, as stipulated by its articles of incorporation.
  (2) If a cooperative member withdrawn or expelled from a cooperative owes an obligation to the cooperative, the cooperative may offset the obligation against the refund under paragraph (1).
  (3) The right to request under paragraph (1) shall lapse, unless it is exercised within two years from the date on which the right holder is withdrawn or expelled from a cooperative.

SECTION 2 Incorporation

Article 21 (Authorization for Establishment) (1) In order to establish a cooperative, at least 30 persons qualified for membership shall prepare articles of incorporation as promoters, have the articles of incorporation adopted upon resolution at the inaugural meeting, and obtain authorization therefor from the Special Metropolitan City Mayor, a Metropolitan City Mayor, a Do Governor, or a Special Self-Governing Province Governor (hereinafter referred to as a "Mayor/Do Governor") having jurisdiction over its business territory under Article 5. If a cooperative's business territory stretches over at least two Cities/Dos, the cooperative shall obtain authorization from the Mayor/Do Governor having jurisdiction over its principal place of business.
  (2) A resolution at the inaugural meeting shall be adopted with the attendance of a majority of persons who have submitted a written consent to establishment (hereinafter referred to as "persons consenting to establishment") to promoters before opening the inaugural meeting and by concurrent votes of at least 2/3 of the persons present at the meeting.
  (3) When a Mayor/Do Governor authorizes the establishment of a cooperative under paragraph (1), he or she shall immediately notify the Fair Trade Commission of such fact.
  (4) The minimum number of persons consenting to establishment, the total amount of equity, and the minimum amount of equity per capita required to establish a cooperative, and other matters such as the standards and procedure for authorization, shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Mar. 29, 2016>

Article 22 (Registration for Incorporation) (1) Authorization to establish a cooperative shall become invalid, unless the establishment of the cooperative is registered within three months from the date such authorization is granted.
  (2) Matters necessary for the registration for establishment under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 23 (Articles of Incorporation) (1) A cooperative's articles of incorporation shall stipulate the following information:
  1. Objectives;
  2. Name;
  3. Business area;
  4. The location of the principal office;
  5. Qualification for membership and proxy;
  6. Matters regarding admission, withdrawal, and expulsion of cooperative members;
  7. The value per equity share, the method and time for the payment of equity shares, and matters regarding the transfer of equity shares;
  8. Matters regarding the appropriation of surplus earnings and the write-off of losses;
  9. Matters regarding the methods for accumulation and use of reserves;
  10. Matters regarding the imposition and collection of expenses, etc.;
  11. Matters regarding the full number, election, and removal of executive officers and representatives;
  12. Matters regarding the appointment and dismissal of officers;
  13. Types of business services and matters regarding the provision of business services;
  14. Matters regarding the fiscal year and accounting;
  15. Matters relating to the method of public announcement;
  16. Matters regarding investment in kind, if acceptable;
  17. The period of existence or the grounds for dissolution, if the period of existence or the grounds for dissolution are stipulated;
  18. Other matters necessary for the operation of the general assembly and the board of directors.
  (2) The Fair Trade Commission may establish and publicly notify standard articles of incorporation.
  (3) No amendment to articles of incorporation shall be effective, unless it is authorized by the Mayor/Do Governor who has authorized the establishment.

Article 24 (Bylaws or Regulations) Except as stipulated in articles of incorporation, matters necessary for the operation of a cooperative and the provision of business services may be prescribed by bylaws or regulations.

SECTION 3 Organs

Article 25 (General Meetings) (1) There shall be organized a general meeting in a cooperative.
  (2) General meetings shall be comprised of cooperative members.
  (3) The president shall convene general meetings and shall preside over such general meetings.
  (4) An annual general meeting shall be convened once a year at the time stipulated in articles of incorporation while an extraordinary general meeting may be convened whenever deemed necessary under articles of incorporation.
  (5) The president shall determine the purposes, agenda items, date, time, and venue of a general meeting by not later than seven days before opening the general meeting and shall give notice that the general meeting is convened by the method stipulated by articles of incorporation.

Article 26 (Matters Subject to Resolution at General Meeting) (1) The following matters shall be subject to resolution at a general meeting: <Amended on Mar. 29, 2016>
  1. Amendments to the articles of incorporation.
  2. Establishment, amendment, or repeal of bylaws;
  3. Election and removal of an executive officer;
  4. Approval of business plans and budgets;
  5. Approval of reports on the settlement of accounts;
  6. Approval of audit reports;
  7. Merger, division, dissolution, or temporary closure of the cooperative;
  8. Expulsion of cooperative members;
  9. Determination of ceiling on borrowings;
  10. Other matters that the president or the board of directors deems necessary.
  (2) The maximum amount of borrowings by a health and medical cooperative shall not exceed the limit set by Presidential Decree in consideration of the total amount of equity of the cooperative, etc. <Newly Inserted on Mar. 29, 2016>

Article 27 (Quorum for Proceedings and Resolutions and Exercise of Voting Rights on Resolutions at General Meetings) (1) Except as otherwise provided in this Act, a general meeting shall be duly formed with the attendance of a majority of all cooperative members, and a resolution shall be adopted by concurrent votes of a majority of the cooperative members present at the meeting. <Amended on Dec. 7, 2021>
  (2) A resolution may be adopted at a general meeting only on the matters notified in advance pursuant to Article 25 (5): Provided, That this shall not apply in emergencies where a resolution is adopted with the attendance of at least 2/3 of all cooperative members and by concurrent votes of at least 2/3 of the cooperative members present at the meeting.
  (3) With regard to a matter in which a cooperative member's interest conflicts with that of the cooperative, the cooperative member shall have no right to vote on a resolution.
  [Title Amended on Dec. 7, 2021]

Article 27-2 (Exercise of Right to Vote on Resolutions and in Elections in Writing or by Electronic Means) (1) Where a cooperative member is unable to attend a general meeting in person and to exercise his or her right to vote on resolutions and in elections due to a disaster under Article 3 of the Framework Act on the Management of Disasters and Safety (hereinafter referred to as "disaster"), he or she may exercise such rights in writing or by electronic means, as prescribed by articles of incorporation. In such cases, the cooperative member shall be deemed present at a general meeting.
  (2) Where a cooperative member is unable to attend a general meeting in person and to exercise his or her right to vote on resolutions and in elections due to a disaster, a resolution may be adopted at a general meeting in writing or by electronic means.
  (3) When the president gives notice of convening a general meeting under Article 25 (5), he or she shall notify cooperative members that they can exercise their right to vote on resolutions and in elections under paragraph (1). In such cases, the president shall attach to such notice the documents and reference materials necessary for cooperative members to exercise such rights.
  (4) A cooperative shall keep documents or electronic records regarding the exercise of the rights to vote on resolutions and in elections for perusal for three months from the date of the closing of a general meeting and shall retain them for five years from the date of the closing of a general meeting.
  (5) Procedures for exercising rights to vote on resolutions and in elections in writing or by electronic means, such as procedures for identifying cooperative members, and other necessary matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Newly Inserted on Dec. 7, 2021]

Article 28 (Matters Subject to Special Resolution at General Meetings) A matter regarding the merger, division, or dissolution of a cooperative shall be subject to resolution with the attendance of a majority of all cooperative members and by concurrent votes of at least 2/3 of the cooperative members present at the meeting.

Article 29 (Minutes of General Meeting) With regard to proceedings of a general meeting, minutes of the meeting shall be prepared to record the course and results of the proceedings, and the president and at least three cooperative members elected at the general meeting or members of the election committee formed pursuant to Article 34 (limited to cases where executive officers or representatives are elected) shall write their names and affix their seals thereto.

Article 30 (General Meeting of Representatives) (1) If the number of cooperative members exceeds that specified by Presidential Decree, a general meeting may be substituted by a general meeting of representatives.
  (2) A general meeting of representatives shall be comprised of representatives elected from among members.
  (3) No representative shall exercise his or her right to vote on resolutions and in elections by proxy.
  (4) The full number, the term of office, and the method of election of representatives shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (5) The provisions governing the general meeting shall apply mutatis mutandis to the general meeting of representatives, and "cooperative member" in such cases shall be construed as "representative": Provided, That the general meeting of representatives shall have no authority to adopt a resolution on a matter regarding the merger, division, or dissolution of the cooperative.

Article 31 (Executive Officers) (1) A cooperative shall have at least seven but not exceeding 20 directors, including one president, and two auditors.
  (2) The full number of directors and the method of electing directors and auditors shall be stipulated by articles of incorporation.
  (3) The president shall be elected from among directors at a general meeting, as stipulated by articles of incorporation.
  (4) Executive officers of a health and medical cooperative shall meet the following requirements: <Newly Inserted on Mar. 29, 2016>
  1. The number of directors related by blood or marriage prescribed by Presidential Decree shall not exceed 1/5 of the total number of directors on the register;
  2. No auditor shall be related, by blood or marriage, to any director of the cooperative, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 32 (Term of Office for Executive Officers) (1) The term of office of executive officers shall be stipulated in articles of incorporation and shall not exceed four years.
  (2) Executive officers may be reappointed for consecutive terms: Provided, That a president may be reappointed for one further term only once.
  (3) The term of office of an executive officer elected to fill a vacancy shall expire at the end of the term of office of his or her predecessor.

Article 33 (Restrictions on Election Campaign) (1) No person shall do any of the following acts for the purpose of causing himself or herself or any specific person to succeed or fail in an election of an executive officer or representative of a cooperative:
  1. Any of the following acts done for a cooperative member (including a person who has filed an application for membership in a cooperative: the same shall apply hereafter in this Article) or any of his or her family members or for an institution, organization, or facility established and operated by a cooperative member or any of his or her family members:
    (a) Offering money, goods, entertainment, or any other interest in property;
    (b) Providing a public or private job;
    (c) Expressing his or her intention to offer money, goods, entertainment, or any other interest in property or to provide a government or private job, or promising to offer such favor;
  2. Committing an act under any item of subparagraph 1 against a person who intends to become a candidate or who is a candidate with intent to have the person fail to become a candidate or to have the person resign from the candidate;
  3. Receiving any benefit or job as referred to in subparagraph 1 or 2, accepting the expression of an intention to provide such benefit or job, or demanding or arranging the provision thereof.
  (2) No person who intends to become an executive officer or representative shall visit cooperative members from door to door or solicit cooperative members to gather in a specific place for an election campaign from the announcement date of an election to an election day. <Amended on Dec. 8, 2020>
  (3) No person shall slander a candidate by publishing any false information or disclosing any fact publicly in a speech or by poster or any other means in connection with an election of an executive officer or representative of a cooperative.
  (4) No person shall conduct an election campaign by any means, other than the following means, in connection with an election of an executive officer or representative: <Amended on May 22, 2013>
  1. Posting propaganda posters;
  2. Distribution of election campaign bulletins;
  3. Distributing printed leaflets;
  4. Holding joint speeches or public forums;
  5. Soliciting supporters by telephone or computer telecommunications networks.

Article 34 (Organization and Operation of Election Committee) (1) A cooperative may form and operate an election committee so as to ensure fair management of an election of executive officers or representatives.
  (2) Necessary matters regarding the functions, organization, and operation of the election committee may be stipulated by articles of association.

Article 35 (Responsibilities of Executive Officers) (1) Executive officers shall observe this Act, orders issued under this Act, articles of incorporation, by laws or regulations, and resolutions of the general meeting and the board of directors and shall perform their duties in good faith for the benefit of their cooperative.
  (2) Executive officers shall be jointly liable for injuries and losses inflicted by an executive officer on the cooperative or any other person intentionally or by gross negligence (intentionally or by negligence, if inflicted by a standing executive officer) in the course of performing his or her duties.
  (3) Paragraph (2) shall also apply where an executive officer inflicts losses on his or her cooperative or any other person by making a misrepresentation in a report on closing accounts, registration, or public notice.
  (4) If an act referred to in paragraph (2) is done according to a resolution adopted by the board of directors, directors who concurred in the resolution shall also be liable therefor under paragraph (2).
  (5) Any person who participated in a resolution under paragraph (4), but failed to express his or her dissent clearly, shall be deemed to have agreed to the resolution.
  (6) The entitlement to reimbursement under any provision of paragraphs (2) through (5) shall be exercised by the president, if the entitlement is exercised against an auditor or director, by an auditor, if the entitlement is exercised against the president, or by the cooperative members' representative with consent of at least 1/5 of cooperative members, if the entitlement is exercised against all executive officers.

Article 36 (Duties of President and Directors) (1) The president shall represent the cooperative and shall execute its business affairs, as stipulated in its articles of incorporation.
  (2) Directors shall execute business affairs of the cooperative, as stipulated in articles of incorporation, and shall act on behalf of the president in the order stipulated in articles of incorporation, if the president is absent from office.
  (3) Except as provided in paragraph (2) and except where the president delegates his or her authority, no director, other than the president, shall represent the cooperative.

Article 37 (Duties of Auditor) (1) Auditors shall audit the current status of business operations, property, accounting books, documents, etc. of the cooperative at least once a year and shall report the results thereof to the general meeting.
  (2) Auditors may verify and inspect accounting books or documents of the cooperative without prior notice.
  (3) When directors execute a business affair in violation of a statute, articles of incorporation, bylaws, regulations, or a resolution passed at a general meeting, auditors shall demand that the board of directors rectify the violation.
  (4) Auditors may attend a general meeting or a directors' meeting and express their opinions at the meeting.
  (5) Two auditors shall jointly submit an audit report or conduct an audit under paragraphs (1) and (2): Provided, That if auditors have different opinions in submitting an audit report, they may submit such opinions, respectively.
  (6) Articles 391-2, 402, 412-2, 413, and 413-2 of the Commercial Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to auditors' duties.

Article 38 (Auditors' Authority to Represent) When a cooperative does a legal act, such as litigation or contract, with its president or director, auditors shall represent the cooperative.

Article 39 (Dismissal of Executive Officers) (1) Cooperative members may request the cooperative to remove an executive officer with the consent of at least 1/5 of cooperative members. In such cases, a written statement of the grounds for removal shall be submitted to the cooperative.
  (2) When a written statement is submitted under paragraph (1), the cooperative shall notify the relevant executive officer thereof in writing by not later than 10 days prior to a general meeting and shall provide the executive officer with an opportunity to express his or her opinion at the general meeting.
  (3) With regard to removal requested under paragraph (1), a resolution shall be adopted at a general meeting with the attendance of a majority of all cooperative members and by concurrent votes of at least 2/3 of the cooperative members present at the meeting.

Article 40 (Grounds for Disqualification of Executive Officers) (1) Any of the following persons shall be disqualified as an executive officer of a cooperative: <Amended on Mar. 29, 2016; Dec. 31, 2018>
  1. A person under adult guardianship;
  2. Deleted; <Apr. 20, 2021>
  3. One who is not yet reinstated after having been declared bankrupt;
  4. A person in whose case three years have not passed since imprisonment without labor or greater punishment declared by a court was completely executed (including where the execution of such sentence is deemed completed) or since he or she was exempted from such sentence;
  5. A person who was sentenced to the suspension of imprisonment without prison labor or any severer penalty and is still in the period of suspension;
  6. A person for whom the sentence of imprisonment without labor or heavier punishment was suspended and who is still in the period of suspension of the sentence;
  7. A person whose qualification is relinquished or suspended by a court judgment or by any other Act;
  8. A person who was sentenced to a fine of not less than three million won for committing a crime prescribed in Article 303 of the Criminal Act or Article 10 of the Act on Special Cases concerning the Punishment of Sexual Crimes and for whom two years have not passed since the sentence became final and conclusive.
  (2) Where any ground prescribed in paragraph (1) arises, the relevant executive officer shall resign as a matter of course.
  (3) Any decision for which an executive officer who resigns pursuant to paragraph (2) is involved before he or she resigns shall remain in effect.

Article 40-2 (Separate Sentence of Punishment of Fines) A person of concurrent crimes who has committed a crime specified in Article 40 (1) 8 of this Act and any other crime, shall be separately sentenced to fines for respective crimes, notwithstanding Article 38 of the Criminal Act.
  [This Article Newly Inserted on Dec. 31, 2018]

Article 41 (Board of Directors) (1) A cooperative shall have a board of directors.
  (2) The board of directors shall consist of directors, including the president.
  (3) The president shall convene board of directors' meetings and shall presided over such meetings.
  (4) A resolution shall be adopted at a directors' meeting with the attendance of a majority of members and by concurrent votes of a majority of the members present at the meeting.
  (5) No director shall participate in a resolution on a matter in which any of his or her personal interests conflicts with that of the cooperative or a matter related to his or her status.
  (6) Unless otherwise provided in the articles of incorporation, the board of directors may allow all or some of the directors to participate in the adoption of a resolution without being present at a meeting by means of a remote communications system that enables all directors to transmit and receive voice simultaneously. In such cases, the relevant directors shall be deemed present at the meeting. <Newly Inserted on Dec. 7, 2021>
  (7) Other matters necessary for the operation of the board of directors shall be stipulated by the articles of incorporation. <Amended on Dec. 7, 2021>

Article 42 (Matters subject to Resolution by Board of Directors) The following matters shall be subject to resolution by the board of directors:
  1. Matters regarding property of the cooperative and the execution of its business affairs;
  2. Convening of general meetings and agenda items to be tabled at a general meeting;
  3. Establishment, amendment, or repeal of regulations;
  4. Borrowing of required funds;
  5. Preparation of business plans and draft budgets;
  6. Approval for appointment or dismissal of officers;
  7. Acquisition and disposal of fundamental assets;
  8. Matters specified in a statute or articles of incorporation;
  9. Other matters referred to by the president for resolution.

Article 43 (Prohibition of Holding Concurrent Office by Executive Officers) (1) The president shall not hold concurrent office as the president of another cooperative.
  (2) Directors, including the president, shall not hold concurrent office as an auditor.
  (3) No executive officer shall hold concurrent office as an employee of the relevant cooperative.

Article 44 (Duty to Keep Documents) (1) The president shall keep articles of incorporation, bylaws, regulations, minutes of the general meeting and the board of directors, accounting books, and the list of cooperative members at the principal place of business.
  (2) The report on closing accounts shall be kept as the principal place of business at least seven days prior to an annual general meeting.
  (3) Creditors and cooperative members of a cooperative may inspect documents specified in paragraphs (1) and (2) and may request the cooperative to issue copies thereof.

SECTION 4 Business

Article 45 (Types of Business Services) (1) A cooperative may provide the following business services to accomplish its objectives:
  1. Purchasing, manufacturing, processing and providing commodities necessary for the consumption of cooperative members;
  2. Providing services by establishing common facilities necessary for the consumption of cooperative members;
  3. Livelihood improvement programs and educational and cultural programs for cooperative members;
  4. Health and medical services for improving health of cooperative members;
  5. Projects entrusted by the State, a local government, a federation, or a national federation;
  6. Services incidental to those specified in subparagraphs 1 through 5;
  7. Other business services specified by Presidential Decree as necessary for accomplishing a cooperative's objectives.
  (2) Matters necessary to provide business services specified in paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Prime Minister.

Article 46 (Use of Business Services) (1) No one, other than a cooperative member, shall be allowed to use the cooperative's business services: Provided, That this shall not apply to cases specified by Ordinance of the Prime Minister for the smooth management of business services, such as advertisement or disposal of goods in stock.
  (2) The use of business services specified in Article 45 by a person belonging to the same household as a cooperative member does, or another cooperative, or a member of another cooperative, shall be deemed the use by a member of the cooperative.
  (3) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), a health and medical cooperative may provide health and medical services to persons specified by Ordinance of the Prime Minister within the limit of 50/100 of total business services provided. <Amended on Mar. 29, 2016>

Article 46-2 (Establishment of Medical Institutions by Health and Medical Cooperatives) (1) A health and medical cooperative may establish only one medical institution: Provided, That where the health and medical cooperative obtains a separate authorization from the Mayor/Do Governor who has authorized the establishment thereof pursuant to Article 21 after meeting such requirements as the number of cooperative members, the amount of equity, and others, it may establish an additional medical institution.
  (2) Further details regarding the number of cooperative members, the amount of equity, and other requirements necessary to obtain a separate authorization pursuant to the proviso of paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Newly Inserted on Mar. 29, 2016]

SECTION 5 Accounting

Article 47 (Fiscal Year and Accounting) (1) The fiscal year of a cooperative shall be stipulated in articles of incorporation.
  (2) Accounts of a cooperative shall be classified into general accounts and special accounts.
  (3) General accounts shall be comprehensive accounts.
  (4) A special account shall be opened, where a specific project is executed, where a specific fund is managed, or where it is necessary to separate an account from general accounts for any other reason, as stipulated in articles of incorporation.
  (5) A health and medical cooperative shall keep a sales account on health and medical services provided to non-members separate from that on health and medical services provided to its members. <Newly Inserted on Mar. 29, 2016>

Article 48 (Business Plan, Budget, and Closing of Accounts) (1) A cooperative shall prepare a report on the closing of accounts (including a business report, a statement of financial position, an income statement, and a plan for appropriating surplus earnings or a plan for writing off losses) for the preceding year and a business plan and draft budget for the current year within three months after the end of each fiscal year for approval at a general meeting. <Amended on Dec. 7, 2021>
  (2) A cooperative may formulate and execute a temporary budget based on the budget for the preceding year until the business plan and budget referred to paragraph (1) are finally approved at a general meeting. Such temporary budget shall be subject to ex post facto approval at a general meeting.
  (3) If a cooperative revises a business plan and budget finally approved at a general meeting, it shall obtain ex post facto approval for such revision at the general meeting held during the following term: Provided, That if its articles of incorporation provide for different rules thereon, such rules shall apply.

Article 49 (Reserves) (1) If a cooperative has surplus earnings after closing its accounts for a fiscal year, it shall accumulate at least 10/100 of the surplus earnings as statutory reserve until the reserve reaches the amount stipulated in articles of incorporation. In such cases, the minimum amount of such reserve to be stipulated by articles of incorporation shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (2) No cooperative shall use a statutory reserve except where it is used for compensating for losses or where the cooperative is dissolved.

Article 50 (Compensation for Losses and Distribution of Surplus) (1) If a cooperative has a loss after closing its accounts for a fiscal year, it shall compensate for the loss with retained earnings first and then with the statutory reserve, and the remaining deficit, if any, shall be carried over to the following fiscal year.
  (2) A cooperative may distribute surplus earnings left over after compensation for losses under paragraph (1) and accumulating the statutory reserve under Article 49 to cooperative members, as stipulated in articles of incorporation. Surplus earnings in such cases shall be distributed in compliance with the following principles:
  1. Dividends distributed according to the records of the use of business services shall be at least 50/100 of the total amount of dividends;
  2. The rate of dividends for paid-in capital shall not exceed the market interest rate.
  (3) Notwithstanding paragraph (2), a cooperative that provides health and medical services shall not distribute surplus earnings to its members.

Article 51 (Prohibition of Acquisition of Equity Shares) No cooperative shall acquire equity shares of its members or accept such equity shares as subject matter of a pledge except where such acquisition or acceptance results from the exercise of rights.

SECTION 6 Merger, Division, Dissolution, and Liquidation

Article 52 (Merger and Division) (1) A cooperative may be merged or divided upon resolution passed at a general meeting.
  (2) A cooperative surviving or newly established as a consequence of a merger or division shall succeed to rights and obligations of the cooperative dissolved after the merger or division.
  (3) The provisions of Articles 21 through 24 shall apply mutatis mutandis to cooperatives established pursuant to paragraph (1).
  (4) A cooperative surviving a merger or division as referred to in paragraph (1) shall file for revised registration. Matters necessary for the revised registration, in such cases, shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 53 (Dissolution) (1) A cooperative shall be dissolved in any of the following events:
  1. Grounds for dissolution prescribed in the articles of incorporation;
  2. Where the general meeting adopts a resolution in favor of the dissolution;
  3. Where it is merged, divided, or bankrupt;
  4. Revocation of authorization for incorporation.
  (2) If a cooperative is dissolved pursuant to any provision of paragraph (1) 1 through 3, it shall report the fact to the competent Mayor/Do Governor within two weeks from the date of dissolution.

Article 54 (Registration of Dissolution) (1) When a cooperative is dissolved, it shall file for registration thereof within one month.
  (2) Matters necessary for the registration of the dissolution under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 55 (Liquidator) (1) When a cooperative is dissolved, the president shall serve as its liquidator, except where the dissolution results from bankruptcy.
  (2) A liquidator shall investigate the status of property without delay after inauguration; prepare a list of property and a statement of financial position; determine methods for the disposal of the property; and then obtain approval thereof at a general meeting. <Amended on Dec. 7, 2021>
  (3) When administrative affairs for liquidation are complete, the liquidator shall prepare a report on the settlement of accounts without delay and shall obtain approval thereof at a general meeting.
  (4) If a cooperative fails to form a general meeting even after convening a general meeting on at least two occasions in cases under paragraphs (2) and (3), it shall obtain consent from at least 2/3 of its members present at the meeting.

Article 56 (Disposal of Residual Property) If a dissolved cooperative has any residual property after paying off debts, such property shall be distributed to its members by the method of calculation adopted at a general meeting in proportion to the number of equity shares: Provided, That a cooperative that provides health and medical services shall not distribute any residual property upon liquidation to its members.

CHAPTER III FEDERATIONS

SECTION 1 Membership

Article 57 (Qualification for Membership) In order to be qualified for membership in a federation, a cooperative shall have its domicile or place of business within the business territory of the federation.

Article 58 (Withdrawals) (1) A member cooperative may withdraw from the federation by informing the federation of its intent to withdraw, as prescribed by the articles of incorporation. <Amended on Dec. 7, 2021>
  (2) In any of the following cases, a member cooperative shall be automatically withdrawn from the federation:
  1. Where the member cooperative ceases to be qualified for membership;
  2. Where a ground specified in its articles of incorporation arises.

Article 59 (Provisions Applicable Mutatis Mutandis) @Articles 14, 15, 17, 19, and 20 shall apply mutatis mutandis to member cooperatives of a federation. In such cases, "cooperative" shall be construed as "federation"; "cooperative member" as "member cooperative,"; "one cooperative member" in Article 15 (2) as "one member cooperative,"; and "20/100" as "40/100," respectively.

SECTION 2 Incorporation

Article 60 (Authorization for Establishment) (1) In order to establish a federation, at least five cooperatives qualified for membership shall prepare articles of incorporation as promoters, obtain a resolution thereon from the inaugural general meeting, and then obtain authorization therefor from the Fair Trade Commission.
  (2) A resolution at the inaugural meeting shall be adopted with the attendance of a majority of persons who have submitted a written consent to establishment (hereinafter referred to as "persons consenting to establishment") to promoters before opening the inaugural meeting and by concurrent votes of at least 2/3 of the persons present at the meeting.
  (3) The minimum number of cooperatives consenting to establishment and the total amount of equity required for the establishment of a federation under paragraphs (1) and (2), and other matters regarding the standards and procedures for authorization shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 61 (Provisions Applicable Mutatis Mutandis) @Articles 22 through 24 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the establishment of federations. In such cases, "cooperative" shall be construed as "federation"; "cooperative member" as "member cooperative"; "Mayor/Do Governor" as "Fair Trade Commission"; and "cooperative member or proxy" in Article 23 (1) 5 as "member cooperative," respectively.

SECTION 3 Organs

Article 62 (General Meetings) (1) Each federation shall have a general assembly.
  (2) General meetings shall be comprised of representatives, as stipulated in articles of incorporation, and convened by the president.
  (3) Representatives shall be elected from among cooperative members belonging to a member cooperative, but at least one cooperative member shall be elected from each member cooperative.

Article 63 (Executive Officers) (1) A cooperative shall have at least seven and up to 30 directors, including one president, and two auditors.
  (2) Executive officers shall be elected at a general meeting from among any of the following persons:
  1. Cooperative members belonging to a member cooperative;
  2. In cases of persons who are not cooperative members prescribed in subparagraph 1, persons with extensive knowledge of and experience in the affairs of cooperatives. In such cases, the number of directors who are not cooperative members shall not exceed 1/5 of the full number of directors and the number of auditors who are not cooperative members shall not exceed 1/2 of the full number of auditors.
  (3) The full number of executive officers, methods for selecting them, and other necessary matters shall be prescribed by the articles of incorporation.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Dec. 7, 2021]

Article 64 (Provisions Applicable Mutatis Mutandis) @Articles 25 (3) through (5), 26 through 29, 30 (3) and (4), 31 (3) and (4), and 32 through 44 shall apply mutatis mutandis to organs of a federation. In such cases, "cooperative" shall be construed as "federation"; "cooperative member" as "member cooperative"; "1/5" in Article 35 (6) and the former part of Article 39 (1) as "1/3"; "cooperative members" in Articles 27 through 29 and 39 (3) as "representatives"; "cooperative member" in Article 33 as "representative or a cooperative member belonging to a member cooperative"; and "person who has filed an application for membership" as "member of a cooperative that has filed an application for membership," respectively. <Amended on Dec. 7, 2021>

SECTION 4 Business

Article 65 (Types of Business Services) (1) A federation may provide the following business services to accomplish its objectives:
  1. Programs for guidance, support, communication, and coordination of member cooperatives;
  2. Developing commodities to be supplied to member cooperatives and purchasing, processing, manufacturing, and distributing commodities so developed;
  3. Mutual aid programs for member cooperatives or cooperative members belonging to a member cooperative;
  4. Projects for the installation and operation of facilities, such as logistics centers available for the common use by member cooperatives;
  5. Offering education and training programs to cooperative members and employees of member cooperatives and providing information to them;
  6. Programs for granting or arranging subsidies to member cooperatives;
  7. Programs for raising and managing financial resources to support the business of member cooperatives;
  8. Projects entrusted or subsidized by the State, a local government, or a national federation;
  9. Services incidental to those specified in subparagraphs 1 through 8;
  10. Other services approved by the Fair Trade Commission as necessary for accomplishing a federation's objectives.
  (2) Matters necessary to provide business services specified in paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Prime Minister.

Article 66 (Mutual Aid Regulations) (1) In order to implement a mutual aid program, a federation shall establish mutual aid regulations and obtain authorization therefor from the Fair Trade Commission. Any amendment thereto shall also require authorization from the Fair Trade Commission.
  (2) Mutual aid regulations referred to in paragraph (1) shall provide for the method of the implementation of a mutual aid program, mutual aid agreements, mutual aid premiums, etc., as prescribed by the Fair Trade Commission.
  (3) The Fair Trade Commission may formulate and enforce standards necessary for the supervision of mutual aid programs to ensure the robust development of mutual aid programs and the protection of contracting parties.

Article 67 (Use of Business Services) (1) No federation shall allow any person, other than a member cooperative, to use its business services: Provided, That this shall not apply to cases specified by Ordinance of the Prime Minister for the smooth management of business services, such as advertisement or disposal of goods in stock.
  (2) The use of business services by a member of a member cooperative shall be deemed the use by the member cooperative.

SECTION 5 Accounting

Article 68 (Provisions Applicable Mutatis Mutandis) @Articles 47 through 49, 50 (1) and (2), and 51 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the accounting for a federation. In such cases, "cooperative" shall be construed as "federation"; and "cooperative member" as "member cooperative," respectively.

SECTION 6 Merger, Division, Dissolution, and Liquidation

Article 69 (Provisions Applicable Mutatis Mutandis) @Articles 52 through 56 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the merger, division, dissolution, and liquidation of a federation. In such cases, "cooperative" shall be construed as "federation"; "cooperative member" as "member cooperative"; "Mayor/Do Governor" as "Fair Trade Commission"; "provisions of Articles 21 through 24" in Article 52 (3) as "Articles 60 and 61"; and "cooperative members" in Article 55 (4) as "representatives," respectively.

CHAPTER IV NATIONAL FEDERATION

SECTION 1 Membership

Article 70 (Classification of National Federations and Qualifications for Membership) National federations shall be classified as follows:
  1. Joint national federation of consumer cooperatives: A national federation whose members are comprised of cooperatives and federations;
  2. National federation of health and medical cooperatives: A national federation whose members are comprised of health and medical cooperatives and federations whose members consist of health and medical cooperatives;
  3. National federation of cooperatives other than health and medical cooperatives: A national federation whose members are comprised of cooperatives other than health and medical cooperatives and federations whose members consist of cooperatives other than health and medical cooperatives.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Dec. 7, 2021]

Article 71 (Provisions Applicable Mutatis Mutandis) @Articles 14, 15, 17, 19, 20, and 58 shall apply mutatis mutandis to members of a national federation. In such cases, "cooperative" shall be construed as "national federation"; "cooperative member" as "member cooperative"; "one cooperative member" in Article 15 (2) as "one member"; and "20/100" as "40/100," respectively.

SECTION 2 Incorporation

Article 72 (Authorization for Establishment) (1) In order to establish a national federation, federations or cooperatives shall prepare articles of incorporation as promoters, obtain a resolution thereon at the inaugural general meeting, and then obtain authorization therefor from the Fair Trade Commission.
  (2) Where a federation that is qualified for membership in a national federation classified under the subparagraphs of Article 70 becomes a promoter, the total number of promoters necessary for the establishment of a national federation under paragraph (1) shall be at least 15 cooperatives, which is the sum of the number of cooperatives belonging to the relevant federation participating in establishment as a promoter and cooperatives that do not belong to any federation participating therein as a promoter but participate in establishment as promoters, and the total number of cooperatives consenting to establishment shall be at least 1/2 of the number of all authorized cooperatives that are qualified for membership in a national federation classified under the subparagraphs of Article 70. In such cases, if a federation submits a written consent to the establishment, the cooperatives belonging to the federation shall be deemed to have submitted a written consent thereto. <Amended on Dec. 7, 2021>
  (3) A resolution at the inaugural general meeting shall be adopted with the attendance of a majority of cooperatives consenting to establishment and by concurrent votes of at least 2/3 of the cooperatives present at the meeting. If a federation attends the inaugural general meeting and exercises its voting right at the meeting, the cooperatives belonging to the federation shall be deemed to attend the inaugural general meeting and exercise their voting rights at the meeting.
  (4) The total amount of equity required for the establishment of a national federation under paragraphs (1) through (3) and other matters regarding the standards and procedure for authorization shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 73 (Provisions Applicable Mutatis Mutandis) @Articles 22 through 24 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the establishment of a national federation. In such cases, "cooperative" shall be construed as "national federation"; "cooperative member" as ""member cooperative"; "Mayor/Do Governor" as "Fair Trade Commission"; and "cooperative member or proxy" in Article 23 (1) 5 as "member cooperative," respectively.

SECTION 3 Organs

Article 74 (General Meetings) (1) A national federation shall hold general meetings.
  (2) General meetings shall be comprised of representatives, as stipulated in articles of incorporation, and convened by the president.
  (3) Representatives shall be elected from among cooperative members belonging to a cooperative or federation, which is a member, and at least one cooperative member shall be elected from each member.

Article 75 (Executive Officers) (1) A national federation shall have at least seven and up to 30 directors, including one president, and two auditors. <Amended on Dec. 7, 2021>
  (2) Executive officers shall be elected at a general meeting from among persons who fall under any of the following: <Newly Inserted on Dec. 7, 2021>
  1. Cooperative members belonging to a cooperative or federation;
  2. Cooperative members belonging to a federation, which is a member;
  3. In cases of persons who are not members prescribed in subparagraph 1 or 2, persons with extensive knowledge of and experience in the affairs of cooperatives. In such cases, the number of directors who are not members shall not exceed 1/5 of the full number of directors and the number of auditors who are not members shall not exceed 1/2 of the full number of auditors.
  (3) The full number of executive officers, methods for selecting them, and other necessary matters shall be prescribed by the articles of incorporation. <Newly Inserted on Dec. 7, 2021>
  (4) The president of a national federation shall not hold concurrent office as the president of a cooperative or federation: Provided, That this shall not apply to the president at the time of establishment. <Amended on Dec. 7, 2021>

Article 76 (Provisions Applicable Mutatis Mutandis) @Articles 25 (3) through (5), 26 through 29, 30 (3) and (4), 31 (3) and (4), 32 through 42, 43 (2) and (3), and 44 shall apply mutatis mutandis to organs of a national federation. In such cases, "cooperative" shall be construed as "national federation"; "cooperative member" as "member"; "1/5" in Article 35 (6) and the former part of Article 39 (1) as "1/3"; "cooperative member" in Articles 27 through 29 and 39 (3) as "representative"; "cooperative member" in Article 33 as "representative or a cooperative member belonging to a member cooperative"; and "person who has filed an application for membership" as "cooperative member belonging to a federation or cooperative that has filed an application for membership," respectively. <Amended on Dec. 7, 2021>

SECTION 4 Business

Article 77 (Types of Business Services) (1) A national federation may provide the following business services to accomplish its objectives:
  1. Services specified in Article 65 (1) 1 through 4, 6, and 7;
  2. Programs for training specialized human resources necessary for the operation of cooperatives or federations;
  3. Projects for research and study on cooperatives, etc., and publicity of cooperatives or federations;
  4. Projects delegated, entrusted, or subsidized by the State or a local government;
  5. Services incidental to those specified in subparagraphs 1 through 4;
  6. Other services approved by the Chairperson of the Fair Trade Commission as necessary for accomplishing the national federation's objectives.
  (2) A national federation may make recommendations to the State, a local government, or a public organization with respect to matters necessary for the promotion of common interests of its members or the development of members.
  (3) Matters necessary to provide business services specified in paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Prime Minister.

Article 78 (Provisions Applicable Mutatis Mutandis) @Articles 66 and 67 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the business services of a national federation. In such cases, "federation" shall be construed as "national federation"; and "cooperative" as "cooperative or federation," respectively.

SECTION 5 Accounting

Article 79 (Provisions Applicable Mutatis Mutandis) @Articles 47 through 49, 50 (1) and (2), and 51 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the accounting of a national federation. In such cases, "cooperative" shall be construed as "national federation"; and "cooperative member" as "member cooperative," respectively.

SECTION 6 Merger, Division, Dissolution, and Liquidation

Article 80 (Provisions Applicable Mutatis Mutandis) @Articles 52 through 55 and the main clause of Article 56 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the merger, division, dissolution, and liquidation of a national federation. In such cases, "cooperative" shall be construed as "national federation"; "cooperative member" as "member cooperative"; "Mayor/Do Governor" as "Fair Trade Commission"; "provisions of Articles 21 through 24" in Article 52 (3) as "Articles 72 and 73"; and "cooperative members" in Article 55 (4) as "representatives," respectively.

CHAPTER V SUPERVISION

Article 81 (Supervision and Entrustment of Authority) (1) A Mayor/Do Governor (referring to the Mayor/Do Governor who has authorized establishment; the same shall apply hereafter in this Chapter) may supervise business operations of each cooperative and issue orders necessary therefor, as provided in this Act.
  (2）The Fair Trade Commission may supervise business operations of each federation and national federation and issue orders necessary therefor, as provided in this Act: Provided, That part of such supervision duties may be delegated to each Mayor/Do Governor, if necessary.
  (3) In any of the following cases, a Mayor/Do Governor may require a cooperative (including a cooperative undergoing incorporation; the same shall apply hereafter in this Article) to report matters regarding its business and property or may authorize public officials under his or her control to inspect the current status of its business, accounting books, and documents and other necessary matters:
  1. Where it is necessary to ascertain whether a cooperative complies with the procedure for establishment or meets the standards for authorization under Article 21;
  2. Where it is necessary to ascertain whether a cooperative violates this Act, an order issued under this Act, or articles of incorporation;
  3. Where it is necessary to ascertain whether a cooperative that provides health and medical services violates the Medical Service Act.
  (4) A public official who conducts an inspection pursuant to paragraph (3) shall carry a certificate indicating his or her authority and present it to interested persons.
  (5) If a Mayor/Do Governor discovers, upon supervision under paragraph (1), that a cooperative violates an order issued under this Act or articles of incorporation, he or she may order the cooperative to take measures for rectification.
  (6) If the Fair Trade Commission deems it necessary for the efficient enforcement of this Act and the formulation of policies on cooperatives, it may require a Mayor/Do Governor to conduct an investigation, inspection, or verification with regard to a cooperative, to demand that a cooperative submit data or take measures necessary for rectification.
  (7) If deemed necessary for the efficient enforcement of this Act and the robust growth and development of cooperatives, the Fair Trade Commission or a Mayor/Do Governor may entrust part of supervision duties to a national federation established pursuant to this Act or to the National Health Insurance Service provided in Article 13 of the National Health Insurance Act, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Mar. 29, 2016>
  [Title Amended on Mar. 29, 2016]

Article 82 (Revocation of Authorization for Establishment) (1) In any of the following cases, a Mayor/Do Governor may revoke authorization for the establishment of a cooperative:
  1. Where it is discovered that the social cooperative has obtained authorization for establishment by fraud or other improper means;
  2. Where a cooperative ceases to meet standards prescribed by Presidential Decree for authorization pursuant to Article 21 (4);
  3. Where a cooperative fails to rectify after receiving an order to take measures for rectification under Article 81 (5);
  4. Where a cooperative fails to commence business without just cause within one year from the date on which its establishment was authorized or has suspended its business continuously for at least one year;
  5. Where a cooperative that provides health and medical services falls under any ground for the revocation of permission for establishing a medical institution under the Medical Service Act.
  (2) Where a Mayor/Do Governor revokes authorization for establishment under paragraph (1), he or she shall publicly notify the fact without delay and shall notify the Fair Trade Commission of the revocation.

Article 83 (Hearings) In order for a Mayor/Do Governor to revoke authorization for the establishment of a cooperative under Article 82 (1), he or she shall hold a hearing.

Article 84 (Provisions Applicable Mutatis Mutandis) (1) Articles 81 (3) through (5), 82 (1), and 83 shall apply mutatis mutandis to federations. In such cases, "cooperative" shall be construed as "federation"; "Mayor/Do Governor" as "Fair Trade Commission"; "Article 21" as "Article 60"; and "Article 21 (4)" as "Article 60 (3)," respectively.
  (2) Articles 81 (3) through (5), 82 (1), and 83 shall apply mutatis mutandis to a national federation. In such cases, "cooperative" shall be construed as "national federation"; "Mayor/Do Governor" as "Fair Trade Commission"; and "Article 21" as "Article 72," respectively.

CHAPTER VI PENALTY PROVISIONS

Article 85 (Penalty Provisions) (1) If an executive officer, employee, or liquidator of a cooperative or federation inflicts a loss on a cooperative by appropriating the cooperative's funds for any purpose other than the cooperative's business purposes or by disposing of or using the cooperative's property, such person shall be punished by imprisonment with labor for not more than 10 years, by a fine not exceeding thirty million won, or both concurrently.
  (2) If an executive officer, employee, or liquidator of a cooperative or federation falls under any of the following subparagraphs, such person shall be punished by imprisonment with labor for not more than three years or by a fine not exceeding 30 million won: <Amended on Oct. 15, 2014; Mar. 29, 2016>
  1. Failing to obtain authorization for a matter subject to authorization by supervisory authorities;
  2. Violating any provision of Articles 46 (3), 48 (1), 49 through 51, 55, and the proviso of Article 56;
  3. Filing for registration by fraud or other improper means;
  4. Executing a matter subject to resolution at a general meeting under this Act without such resolution.

Article 86 (Penalty Provisions) (1) Any of the following persons shall be punished by imprisonment with labor for up to two years or by a fine not exceeding 20 million won: <Amended on Oct. 15, 2014>
  1. A person who participates in an election of public officials, in violation of Article 7 (2);
  2. A person who conducts an election campaign, in violation of Article 33 (1) (including cases applicable mutatis mutandis under Article 64 or 76).
  (2) Any of the following persons shall be punished by imprisonment with labor for not more than one years or by a fine not exceeding 10 million won: <Amended on Aug. 15, 2014>
  1. A person who visits people from door to door or solicits people to gather at a specific place, in violation of Article 33 (2) (including cases applicable mutatis mutandis under Article 64 or 76);
  2. A person who conducts an election campaign, in violation of Article 33 (4) (including cases applicable mutatis mutandis under Article 64 or 76).
  (3) Any person who slanders a candidate by publishing any false information or by disclosing any fact publicly, in violation of Article 33 (3) (including cases applicable mutatis mutandis under Article 64 or 76) shall be punished by a fine between three million won and 20 million won.
  (4) The period of prescription for the public prosecution of a crime specified in any of paragraphs (1) through (3) shall expire upon lapse of six months after the relevant election date: Provided, the period shall expire upon lapse of three years if the offender is a fugitive.

Article 87 (Joint Penalty Provisions) If an executive officer, employee, or liquidator of a cooperative or federation commits an offense under Article 85 in connection with the business affairs of the cooperative or federation, not only shall such offender be punished accordingly, but also the cooperative or federation shall be punished by a fine under the applicable provisions: Provided, That this shall not apply where such cooperative or federation has not been negligent in giving due attention and supervision concerning the relevant business affairs to prevent such offense.

Article 88 (Administrative Fines) (1) Any person who violates Article 4 (2) shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding five million won.
  (2) If a cooperative or federation violates any of the following, it shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding three million won: <Amended on Mar. 29, 2016>
  1. If a cooperative fails to indicate the fact that its own medical institution has been founded by a cooperative, in violation of Article 4 (3);
  2. If a cooperative permits a cooperative member to hold equity shares in excess of 20/100 of the total number of equity shares of the cooperative (40/100 in cases to which this subparagraph applies mutatis mutandis under Article 59 or 71), in violation of Article 15 (2) (including cases applicable mutatis mutandis under Article 59 or 71);
  3. If a cooperative gives unequal right to vote on resolutions or in elections to cooperative members according to the number of equity shares, in violation of Article 16 (1);
  4. If a cooperative or federation permits any person, other than a cooperative member or a member cooperative or federation, to use the business services of the cooperative or federation, in violation of Article 46 (1) or 67 (1) (including cases applicable mutatis mutandis under Article 78).
  (3) If an executive officer, employee, or liquidator of a cooperative or federation falls under any of the following subparagraphs, such person shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding one million won: <Amended on Mar. 29, 2016>
  1. Neglecting to file for registration;
  2. If he or she makes a false statement or submits a false report to a supervisory agency or the general assembly, or conceals a fact;
  3. If he or she refuses, interferes with, or evades an inspection of a supervisory agency.
  4. Failing to keep a sales account on health and medical services provided to non-members separate from that on health and medical services provided to his or her members, in violation of Article 47 (5).
  (4) Administrative fines prescribed in the provisions of paragraphs (1) through (3) shall be imposed and collected by the Minister of Health and Welfare or Mayors/Do Governors, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

ADDENDA <Act No. 10173, Mar. 22, 2010>
Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Act shall enter into force six months after the date of its promulgation.
Article 2 (Transitional Measures concerning Cooperatives, etc.)
(1) If an incorporated association, which is not a cooperative but has already been established for objectives similar to those of a cooperative before this Act enters into force, intends to become a cooperative, it shall fulfill the prerequisites for the establishment of a cooperative, as provided in Article 21 (4), obtain a resolution thereon at a general meeting with the attendance of a majority of partners and by concurrent votes of at least 2/3 of the partners present at the meeting, and then obtain authorization therefor from the competent Mayor/Do Governor. In such cases, "persons consenting to establishment" shall be construed as "partners," "promoters" as "the representative of the association," and "inaugural meeting" as "general meeting," respectively.
(2) If an incorporated association already established for objectives similar to those of a federation before this Act enters into force, intends to become a federation, it shall fulfill the prerequisites necessary for the establishment of a federation, as provided in Article 60, obtain a resolution thereon at a general meeting with the attendance of a majority of partners and by concurrent votes of at least 2/3 of the partners present at the meeting, and then obtain authorization therefor from the Fair Trade Commission. In such cases, "cooperatives consenting to establishment" shall be construed as "partners," "promoters" as "the representative of the association," and "inaugural meeting" as "general meeting," respectively.
(3) If an incorporated association already established for objectives similar to those of a national federation before this Act enters into force, intends to become a national federation, it shall fulfill the minimum number of cooperatives consenting to establishment, as provided for in Article 72 (2), and the prerequisites necessary for the establishment of a national federation, as provided for in Article 72 (4), obtain a resolution thereon at a general meeting with the attendance of a majority of partners and by concurrent votes of at least 2/3 of the partners present at the meeting, and then obtain authorization therefor from the Fair Trade Commission. In such cases, "cooperatives consenting to establishment" shall be construed as "partners"; "promoters" as "the representative of the association"; and "inaugural meeting" as "general meeting," respectively.
Article 3 (Transitional Measure concerning Names)
Article 4 (2) shall not apply, for one year from the date this Act enters into force, to organizations that perform the same functions as cooperatives’ as at the time this Act enters into force, but has not been established pursuant to this Act.
Article 4 (Transitional Measure concerning Term of Office of Cooperative’s Executive Officers)
Executive officers of a cooperative as at the time this Act enters into force shall be deemed executive officers for the purposes of this Act, and their term of office shall expire at the end of the term specified in previous articles of incorporation.
Article 5 (Transitional Measures concerning Administrative Dispositions, etc.)
An act done by or in relation to an administrative agency pursuant to the previous provisions as at the time this Act enters into force shall be deemed an act done by or in relation to an administrative agency pursuant to the relevant provisions of this Act.
Article 6 (Transitional Measures concerning Penalty Provisions and Administrative Fines)
An act committed before this Act enters into force shall be governed by a former provision in applying penalty provisions and imposing administrative fines.
Article 7 (Relationships to other Statutes)
A citation of provisions of the previous Consumer Cooperatives Act by any other statute in force as at the time this Act enters into force shall be deemed a citation of the corresponding provisions of this Act in lieu of the previous provisions, if such corresponding provisions exist in this Act.
